title: The third fleet's first tank-hull reaches Ceann mhòr
summary: A week after its raising at Baile ghorm the third fleet's first tank-hull, her number chalked on her bow for want of a name, comes into Ceann mhòr with the army's dubhan. Her master, Griogair, a fisherman of Baile ghorm forty years, talks with Corporal Dùghall mac Iain on the quay through the unloading.

title: Dùghall billeted on Barbara
summary: At Ceann mhòr Dùghall mac Iain is billeted on a Tuathaich widow named Barbara, who feeds him at her own table and answers him only in Dia-thìris, though he hears her, of an evening, singing at her loom in the humans' tongue she will not use to speak to him directly.

title: A file sent north to Baile chrom
summary: The fourth regiment sends Corporal Dùghall mac Iain and six men on the two days' coast road to Baile chrom, a bent headland town no patrol of the regiment has yet troubled to search, with orders to look for arms and for men of the western hills and to bring back a report.

title: The watched mill on the coast road
summary: On the march north the file passes a mill and two farms whose people watch them from their doorways and say nothing, a silence the soldier Cailean judges more telling, in its own way, than any shout a Dia-thìreach farm on the same road would have raised.

title: The town found dark and silent
summary: Dùghall mac Iain's file comes into Baile chrom after dark on the eve of the Grey Night to find no lamp lit, no dog loosed and every door unlatched; house after house holds a family sitting hands folded round a cold hearth, answering nothing but a single slow headshake.

title: Margaret Crane keeps the vigil alone
summary: In the house nearest the lighthouse road an old woman named Margaret Crane sits alone keeping the Grey Night as she has kept it since before the war, gives Dùghall mac Iain her name and leave to search, and tells him nothing more; a soldier of his own file sets his lamp down outside her door rather than carry its light past her.

title: The regimental clerk's question
summary: Copying Dùghall mac Iain's report fair at the bothy, the file's young clerk asks whether there is more to the night than its three written lines; Dùghall tells him there is not, and keeps the headshakes and the cold hearths out of the regiment's own returns.

title: Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg open their roads
summary: A week after Dùghall mac Iain's report goes in, the last two of the five holdout towns open their roads to the regiments without a siege; their pits are flooded the same day, and the open record names no holdout taken at either, the same three words standing where a longer account might have stood.

title: Barbara on the flooded pits
summary: Dùghall mac Iain mentions the flooding of Àth naomh's pits to Barbara over her evening table; she answers only, in Dia-thìris, that a pit flooded is a pit flooded whichever order floods it, and takes up her mending again in the silence he has learned by then not to press.

title: The ninth regiment raised at the southern Seann Skell
summary: On Christmas Day the ninth regiment is raised at the southern Seann Skell to guard the shipmasters' dubhan works; word of it reaches Ceann mhòr's guardroom two days after, one more line in a winter Dùghall mac Iain has come to measure by such lines alone.

title: Dùghall's sleepless winter
summary: Through the short days that follow, Dùghall mac Iain wakes most nights with the sea-sound of the Baile chrom headland in his ears, unable in either tongue he carries to find words for a stillness that asked nothing of him and gave him nothing to answer with.

title: The file sent round by the headland farms
summary: Corporal Dùghall mac Iain's file of six is sent to Baile chrom by way of the headland farms, sleeping a night in an empty drover's bothy on the way.

title: Cailean says the house searched him back
summary: Marching back from Baile chrom, a soldier named Cailean says he has never come away from a search feeling the house had searched him back, and would not go north again.

title: The ninth's raising read at Ceann mhòr
summary: Two days after an Nollaig the raising of the ninth regiment at the southern Seann Skell is read out in the fourth regiment's guardroom at Ceann mhòr.
